He is up to date on all vaccines and is meeting all developmental milestones. On physical exam, he is noted to have a right upper extremity blood pressure of 150/80 mm Hg. 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses are felt. Cardiac auscultation reveals a regular rate and rhythm with a normal S1 and S2. A 2/6 long systolic murmur with systolic ejection click is heard over left sternal border and back. First, the child is 5 years old and had a well-child visit. His mother says he's doing well and has no concerns. That means there are no obvious symptoms or issues she's noticing. He was born at 39 weeks via spontaneous vaginal delivery, which is normal and not preterm. He's up to date on vaccines and meeting all developmental milestones, so no delays there. On physical exam, the right upper extremity blood pressure is 150/80 mm Hg. That seems high because, for a child, normal blood pressure can vary, but generally, a BP of 150/80 might be elevated. However, I should check what's considered normal for a 5-year-old. I think the normal range is around 100-120 mmHg for systolic and 60-80 for diastolic, so 150 is definitely high. He has 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses. Radial pulses are in the arms, and femoral are in the groin. 2+ might be normal, but trace could indicate something is a bit off. Maybe decreased femoral pulses could suggest something like coarctation of the aorta, which can cause reduced pulse strength in the lower extremities. A systolic murmur is heard between S1 and S2, and a ejection click is a click that occurs just after S1, often associated with aortic stenosis or sclerosis, or maybe a bicuspid aortic valve. The pulses are weaker in the femoral area, which might indicate a narrowing somewhere in the aorta, like coarctation.
